title: Overshadowing of an adjoining property at midday 21 June, climate zones 4 to 6 (25% / 35% / 50% / nil by adjoining coding)
text: Development in climate zones 4, 5 and 6 shall be designed such that the shadow cast at midday on 21st June onto any adjoining property does not exceed: adjoining properties coded R25 and lower - 25% of the site area (1); adjoining properties coded R30 - R40 - 35% of the site area (1); adjoining properties coded R50 - R60 - 50% of the site area (1); adjoining properties coded R80 or higher - Nil requirements. (1) Where a development site shares its southern boundary with a lot, and that lot is bound to the north by other lot(s), the limit of shading at A 3.2.3 shall be reduced proportionally to the percentage of the affected properties northern boundary that abuts the development site.
notes: from: ch4p1 C3.8.1 (Table 3.8a), but here the limits are in the clause and there is no diagonal-lot or narrow-lot limit. 'R80 or higher - Nil requirements': table-3.2-overshadow returns null, so the rule is NOT_APPLICABLE for an adjoining lot coded R80+ or a named apartment code. The adjoining lot is read as adjoining.south (the lot receiving the shadow). Footnote 1 proportional reduction is A3.2.3-r1. Register: Vol 2 Figure A7.2 (proportionate northern boundary limits) deleted with Appendix A7; the draft footnote has no figure. ToC p12 'confirm no maximum overshadowing applies to R80'. Regional: the 25% limit still binds 4-8 storey buildings next to R25-and-lower land.
